title: Disconnected-site POC playbook: patterns, tradeoffs, and workshop runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note collects feasibility findings, recommended deployment patterns, and an actionable workshop/runbook for a customer POC where the target environment is a partially disconnected (intermittent internet) or fully air-gapped on-prem site. The goal is to leave the customer with a reproducible POC that validates inference latency, model pinning/rollout, and secure model artifacts transfer without depending on continuous outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane.

Customer context (summary):
- Industry: regulated healthcare imaging analytics (data residency + PHI).
- Target site characteristics: dual-rack on-prem cluster, private VLANs, no direct internet egress from inference cluster; bastion host permitted for occasional file transfer; customer IT restricts inbound connections and disallows cloud-managed agents.
- Primary POC goals: demonstrate 1) model serving performance with a ~4B parameter open model quantized to int8, 2) model version rollouts and fallback behavior, 3) KMS integration for model keys, and 4) controlled telemetry export with customer approval.

Assumptions made for this document (validate in kickoff):
- Customer can provide a temporary jump-host with limited outbound access (SCP/HTTPS allowed to an internal transfer node).
- Runtimes will be deployed to customer-provided GPU hosts (NVIDIA A10/A100 class) with at least 4 GPUs for the POC.
- Storage: 50–200 GB available for model artifacts and KV caches; NFS or Ceph-backed filesystem optional.
- Security: customer will provide KMS/HSM integration details or accept Redwood-managed envelope encryption for POC artifacts transported via USB if HSM unavailable.

Three recommended disconnected deployment patterns (tradeoffs):
1) Sealed-appliance pattern (fully air-gapped, physical media transfer)
   - Overview: Build a self-contained VM/container image bundle (inference runtime + pinned model shard files + orchestration manifests) delivered on encrypted removable media. Installation done by customer SRE.
   - Pros: no outbound dependency, aligns with strict compliance; simple runtime topology; deterministic artifacts.
   - Cons: slower iteration (each model change requires new media), support limited to asynchronous logs/artifact snapshots, complex KMS exchange.
   - When to pick: high compliance/regulatory requirements, no jump-host allowed.

2) Jump-host assisted pattern (recommended POC baseline)
   - Overview: Small transfer host (jump-host) mediates occasional artifact syncs (HTTPS/SCP to a vetted transfer endpoint). Control plane signals are batched and pulled by the site in scheduled windows using signed manifests.
   - Pros: faster iteration than sealed-appliance; supports delta updates (model diffs), feasible remote troubleshooting via temporarily open port or bastion tunnel under customer control.
   - Cons: requires a vetted transfer process and trust model; telemetry must be explicit and opt-in.
   - When to pick: customer comfortable with scheduled outbound transfers and remote troubleshooting windows.

3) Hybrid mirrored control plane (semi-managed private control plane)
   - Overview: Customer runs a lightweight Redwood control-plane proxy in their private network (VM or k8s service) that exposes the same API as hosted control plane. Periodic signed syncs between Redwood control plane and proxy happen over a customer-controlled channel.
   - Pros: near-hosted UX, supports rollouts and automated health checks, faster incident response.
   - Cons: requires more on-prem expertise, higher operational surface area, longer procurement.
   - When to pick: customer wants feature parity with hosted and will commit to ongoing private control-plane ops.

Minimum POC infra checklist (what we ask customer to provide):
- Compute: 2–4 GPU hosts (A10/A100), Linux 5.x+, >= 64GB RAM each.
- Network: private VLAN for inference cluster, ability to create temporary outbound allow-list entries to internal transfer node or jump-host.
- Storage: shared POSIX filesystem or per-node SSDs; at least 200GB total for models and cache.
- Bastion/jump-host: small VM with SCP/HTTPS and scheduled transfer window (if using jump-host pattern).
- KMS/HSM: endpoint or instructions for wrapping/unwrapping model keys; if unavailable, agree on signed envelope workflow for POC.
- Access: on-site SRE contact; timeboxed remote access window for Redwood engineers (optional, mutually agreed).

Operational considerations and runbook snippets:
- Artifact signing and verification: all model bundles must be signed with Redwood infra key; site validates signatures before install. Include checksum file and signed manifest.
- Model rollout: for jump-host pattern, use versioned manifests and a two-step rollout (stage -> health-check -> promote). Health-checks are executed locally with a small testset (we provide test prompts).
- Telemetry & logs: default policy is no external telemetry. If customer approves, enable batched telemetry over transfer window with PII scrubbers and explicit allowlist.
- Support / incident triage: collect local logs, sysinfo, and a compact trace bundle that can be transferred out-of-band. If remote debugging allowed, use ephemeral reverse-tunnel established from bastion only during low-risk windows.
- Upgrades: minimal viable upgrade process is: upload new signed bundle -> install to staging nodes -> smoke test -> promote. Document rollback steps.

Network and security rules (suggested minimal ACLs):
- Inference nodes: deny inbound internet. Allow NFS/Ceph and internal control-plane proxy traffic. Block outbound except to internal transfer node IPs + internal auth services.
- Jump-host: allow outbound to Redwood transfer endpoint (HTTPS over 443) and SSH/SCP to internal admin network; restrict creds to local SRE.
- Bastion: allow ephemeral inbound from Redwood IPs during scheduled windows and log all sessions.

Data flow patterns for model updates and telemetry:
- Model update (jump-host): Redwood -> signed artifact -> push to transfer node -> site pulls -> install -> local smoke tests -> mark version active in local manifest.
- Model update (sealed-appliance): physical media -> SRE copies -> local verification -> install.
- Telemetry (opt-in): local aggregator writes daily compressed batch to transfer node. Manual approval required per batch.

KMS/key management options (POC-friendly):
- Customer HSM: Redwood provides the encrypted model bundle; customer unwraps using HSM-provided keys during install.
- Envelope encryption: Redwood encrypts model with per-POC symmetric key; customer manages key locally. Key exchange: use out-of-band signed token delivered via transfer host or physical media.
- Short-term fallback: for POC only, we can use password-protected archives with strict retention policy (documented and agreed).

POC success criteria (measurable):
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency <= 150ms for typical prompt mix at single-concurrent-worker baseline (specify prompts).
- Throughput: sustain X tokens/sec with deterministic batching (define X based on GPUs provided).
- Rollout: demonstrate a model promotion with zero-downtime fallback to previous version within 5 minutes.
- Security: ability to verify model signature and demonstrate encrypted model install flow.
- Observability: local tracing and smoke-test results uploaded via sanctioned transfer window.

Workshop / run-of-show (90–120 minutes onsite or remote hybrid)
- Pre-work (2 weeks before): collect inventory form (host specs, storage, network constraints, KMS options).
- 00:00–00:15: Introductions & POC objectives alignment (SRE, security, ML lead).
- 00:15–00:30: Review chosen deployment pattern and security model; confirm transfer method.
- 00:30–01:00: Hands-on: deploy a minimal inference container on a single node and run smoke prompts (we provide lightweight image).
- 01:00–01:20: Model rollout demo: simulate push of a second version via transfer node and perform staged promotion.
- 01:20–01:40: Failure drills: simulate node loss and verify fallback behavior and integrity checks.
- 01:40–02:00: Next steps, acceptance criteria sign-off, action items, and schedule for final acceptance run.

Risks, mitigations and open constraints:
- Risk: long artifact transfer times for multi-GB models. Mitigation: offer delta-compression + quantized models; pre-warm caches via staging nodes.
- Risk: customer lacks KMS/HSM. Mitigation: secure envelope workflow and strict handling SOP for POC window; escalate to security review for production.
- Risk: support latency when remote access not allowed. Mitigation: detailed runbook, extra validation tests in bundle, and extended knowledge transfer session with SREs.

Open questions (to resolve during kickoff):
- Can customer provide an internal transfer host with scheduled outbound HTTPS? (yes/no)
- Are there policy constraints preventing ephemeral remote tunnels for debugging?
- What is the target throughput objective (tokens/sec) and representative prompt set we should test against?
- Is the site willing to run the Redwood control-plane proxy VM for the POC or prefer sealed-appliance?

Action items (next 10 days):
- SE: produce signed sample model bundle (small demo model) and a step-by-step install guide (target: +3 business days).
- Customer SRE: return inventory form and confirm jump-host availability (+5 business days).
- Security: produce POC data handling agreement and telemetry opt-in template (+5 business days).
- Eng: prepare a compact debug bundle and automated smoke-test suite (+7 business days).

Appendix: artifact checklist for transfer media
- signed-manifest.json (SHA256, signer id)
- model.tar.gz.sig (signature file)
- model.tar.gz.enc (encrypted artifact)
- install.sh (idempotent installer with verification and rollback hooks)
- smoke-tests.json (deterministic prompt set)
- README-security.md (KMS/decryption steps and contact)
_notes: This document is intentionally formatted as a working playbook with checklists, runbook steps, and open questions to be iterated during the customer kickoff. Keep as Drive doc (work-in-progress) until POC acceptance.
